topic: explain RAG: how retrieval-augmented generation works

sources.title: Show HN: Treyspace – A canvas that gives your LLM spatial awareness

facts.statement: RAG combines search with generation instead of relying only on an LLM's memory.
facts.quote: It’s a technique that combines search + generation.

facts.statement: A RAG system retrieves relevant data from external sources such as PDFs or Markdown files.
facts.quote: Retrieves relevant data from external sources (e.g., your PDFs or like in this project i used md(markdown files)

facts.statement: Retrieved information is added to the prompt before the language model generates an answer.
facts.quote: Augments the prompt with this info -- > then Generates a relevant answer using the LLM!

facts.statement: A document loader loads source data including PDFs, text files, and Notion content.
facts.quote: Loads your data (PDFs, text files, Notion, etc.)

facts.statement: A text splitter breaks documents into chunks that fit the model's context size.
facts.quote: Breaks the documents into chunks (to fit context size)

facts.statement: An embedding model converts text chunks into vectors using embedding providers such as OpenAI or Hugging Face.
facts.quote: Converts text chunks into vectors using OpenAI or Hugging Face embeddings

facts.statement: A vector store stores vectorized text and allows it to be searched.
facts.quote: Stores and lets you search vectorized text

facts.statement: The retriever searches for relevant chunks based on the user's query.
facts.quote: Searches for relevant chunks based on the user query

facts.statement: One illustrated RAG architecture flows from a browser through React, FastAPI, an embedding engine, a retriever, a vector database, and an LLM.
facts.quote:
Browser ↓
React
↓
FastAPI
↓
Embedding Engine
↓
Retriever
↓
Vector DB
↓
LLM

facts.statement: The source describes RAG as helping avoid hallucinations, eliminating the need for fine-tuning, and supporting real-time data.
facts.quote:
Avoids hallucination (answers based on your docs, not guesses)
You don’t need to fine-tune a model
Works with real-time data
